findings.claim: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl was not refreshed with the entityfix regate
findings.evidence: Last elf-b5-002 record in verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl is line 30, executed_by 'claude-opus-4-8/G-KEY' (pre-rename vote 2). The four sibling files all end on '*-entityfix' records for this unit.
findings.why: The resolved file is the merged authority for G-KEY; leaving it pre-rename makes the vfinal store internally inconsistent. Non-substantive here because both entityfix votes reproduce the same solver answers (B, A, C, D, B) as the records it still holds.

findings.claim: The entityfix regate introduced a NEW major G-STEM flag at q1 that has no disposition record anywhere
findings.evidence: Pre-rename verdicts/verdicts-gstem.jsonl: q1 pass, q2 pass, q3/q4/q5 flag(major). Post-rename verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gstem.jsonl: q1 flag(major, cross-question corroboration with q5/B), q2 pass, q3/q4/q5 flag(major). ADJUDICATION.md section 'elf-b5-002' lists only q3/q4/q5; reviews/final_verify.jsonl reports gkey/gdistractor counts and is silent on G-STEM.
findings.why: Answer design is provably unchanged (letters, keys and all non-toponym option text byte-identical to pre-rename), so the repair did not create the tell; this is regate judgement variance. It is nonetheless an undocumented change of gate state on a shipped unit.

findings.claim: 'Rosalind Teale ... confirmed clear, kept unchanged' understates that Teale was itself introduced the same day
findings.evidence: candidates/elf-b5-002.json (generator output) names the historian 'Ottilie Brandt'; reviews/pedagogy.jsonl carries a separate 2026-07-30 registry-collision repair renaming Brandt -> Rosalind Teale because elf-b5-001 also uses 'Ottilie Brandt'. git HEAD of candidates-final already reads Teale, so the claim is true relative to the real-entity repair's own baseline.
findings.why: Read on its own the note implies Teale is the original generator name that merely survived a sweep. The claim is accurate in scope but a reader reconstructing provenance from the note alone would be misled.

findings.claim: 'Loddevik' exists as a Norwegian personal surname
findings.evidence: friidrettsresultater.no lists an athlete 'Emil Loddevik' (b. 2009). Kartverket exact and wildcard, OSM/Nominatim, Wikidata and no/en Wikipedia all return 0 for Loddevik as a place.
findings.why: Not a collision in a related domain: the passage uses Loddevik as a 17th-century chart-workshop town, and no toponym of that name exists in any consulted gazetteer. Recorded so the residual is on the record rather than rediscovered later.

findings.claim: General-web exact-phrase confirmation was unavailable this session
findings.evidence: WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200); duckduckgo, duckduckgo-lite and mojeek all returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. Verification therefore rests on Kartverket (exact + wildcard), OSM/Nominatim, Wikidata (entity + full-text), no/en Wikipedia full-text and the Exa index.
findings.why: The gazetteer and knowledge-base checks are the decisive ones for toponyms and notable persons, but a general-index exact-phrase sweep would strengthen the negative result.
